findings.title: ShinyHunters: Cyber Criminal Group Attacks Learning Management System
findings.summary_md: The IC3 public service announcement that is the stated root cause of the FBI attack: it describes ShinyHunters' assault on an online learning management system, details the group's pressure tactics including threatening texts and calls to victims' relatives and swatting, and recommends recipients not pay extortion demands. Date taken from the page's own alert header, Alert Number I-051526-PSA, 15 May 2026, roughly four months before this story's first event.

findings.title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack: 'This is NOT financially motivated'
findings.summary_md: First news coverage, published about two days before this story's first event. It records the group's claims of an Oracle PeopleSoft pre-auth zero-day giving remote code execution on the jobs portal at apply.fbijobs.gov, a 2 TB to 3 TB haul covering current, former, and prospective employees, claimed lateral movement onto FBI-managed AWS GovCloud servers with access to HR, MedLink, and CJIS services, the 'This site has been seized by ShinyHunters' defacement, and the demand that the FBI retract its 15 May bulletin. Timestamp taken from the article's own 'Published Tue 22 Sept 2026 // 17:24 UTC' line.

findings.title: FBI Hack Exposed FBI's Own Hacking Unit
findings.summary_md: Joseph Cox reports that the stolen personnel data includes members of the FBI's Remote Operations Unit, the secretive team that builds exploits and covert-access tools, potentially revealing who is in the unit, and frames the trove as valuable to criminals and foreign intelligence agencies. The full post is paywalled. Exact timestamp taken from the site's RSS feed pubDate.
